    The module of a line is indecomposable #

    For a map of the total space of the line representation satisfying the block equations of the push-down, the diagonal blocks are multiplication by one scalar (dsc_const): the arrows of the line are identities and the line is connected. A map with a zero column therefore has zero diagonal, and the chain argument of Lemma 4.3 (PushDown.Chain, with the block classes of the covering, Proposition 4.4) shows that every endomorphism of the push-down is a scalar plus a nilpotent map. Hence the push-down is indecomposable (isIndecomposable_lineMod).
